sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Ruby interview questions at the intermediate level start with the language itself — the object model that underpins everything, mutability and freeze semantics, the truthiness rules that trip up engineers coming from other languages, and the comparisons interviewers return to in every round (== vs equal? vs eql?, Symbol vs String, freeze vs dup). This page covers the Ruby language fundamentals that map directly to the questions asked in backend engineering interviews at Rails-focused companies. For OOP-specific questions (class hierarchy, duck typing, method lookup) see the Ruby OOP page. For blocks, procs, and lambdas see the dedicated page — that topic demands its own full treatment. Every answer targets Ruby 3.3 idiomatic style: implicit returns, predicate methods with ?, bang methods with !, and safe navigation with &.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: comparisons, object-model, types-and-mutability, string-symbol, scenario-based. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
